P1: The RTX PRO 6000 queue has the most free capacity and needs the newest software. In one measurement, 58 of its 64 GPUs were idle while the A100 queue had 900 jobs pending against 10 free GPUs. The queue is idle because the card is sm_120 and the PyTorch in the conda environments only ships kernels to sm_90. PyTorch runs on the card through driver PTX JIT compilation, but nothing is precompiled for it. On a small fp32 CNN, the measured cost was a one-time JIT delay of about 85 s, then about 5% slower than A100 in steady state. The queue is fine for single-GPU work. It has no NVLink or InfiniBand, so never use it for multi-GPU or multi-node work.
P2: Slack messages always go to the user by default. When asked to "send a slack message", "draft a message", or similar, send or draft it as a DM to the user so they can review and forward it. NEVER send directly to anyone else (collaborators, channels, etc.) unless the user explicitly says "send to <person>" or "post in <channel>". Even then, confirm with the user before sending.
P3: Never install packages into a conda env while a cluster job using that env is still running. Check `bjobs` first. If a job is live, either wait for it to finish, or run `mamba create -n <env>_v2 --clone <env>` and install into the clone. pip can silently replace numpy or scipy on disk underneath the live Python process. Modules that are already imported stay in memory, but anything imported afterwards may load the new version. After ANY env change, immediately run `pip freeze > env/<name>_pinned_requirements.txt` and note the date, so results can be traced to a known package set.
P4: When I say "upload to Google Drive" for a pptx, docx, pdf, or html deliverable and give no folder, the default destination is the team deliverables folder, through the rclone remote `drive:` with `--drive-root-folder-id <ID>`. Before uploading, list the folder and check it for a file with the same name as the one you are uploading. Don't overwrite someone else's file. Stage the files in one local folder, run `rclone copy` on that folder once, then verify with `rclone check --checksum --one-way <stage> drive: --drive-root-folder-id <ID>` and report the matching-file count. Never use `--size-only`.
P5: Codex sends the prompt and every file it reads to OpenAI. This is fine for the user's own analyses. For patient data, embargoed collaborator data, or anything the user marked sensitive, ask the user first. Verify every finding before applying it. Codex is a reviewer and its findings can be wrong, so open the cited file and line and confirm. In one past review, all "must fix" items held up, but Codex's suggested wording sometimes over-corrected. Keep the author's voice and make the minimum effective edit.
